IN PHOTOS: In observance of Holy Week, health workers from various hospitals in Metro Manila staged a "Kalbaryo ng Manggagawang Pangkalusugan at Mamamayan" protest in front of the Department of Health (DOH) on March 31, 2026. 

The demonstration highlighted the worsening conditions they face alongside the Filipino people amid a deepening economic and health crisis. 

The continuing instability in fuel supply has driven up prices, triggering widespread increases in the cost of basic goods and essential commodities—including medicines, hospitalization, and healthcare access—placing an even heavier burden on both health workers and the public.

📸: Norman Cruz

Urban poor groups gathered at the NIA Road Settlement Area in Quezon City on Tuesday, March 31, weeks after a massive fire devastated the community, to launch “Kalbaryo 2026,” an annual Lenten mobilization that transforms the traditional Way of the Cross into a symbol of the urban poor’s continuing struggle against displacement, housing insecurity, and lack of basic services.

Participants carried crosses symbolizing the burden of joblessness, soaring fuel prices, rising cost of living, and the constant threat of eviction. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB

data.raw_text:
In observance of Holy Week, healthcare workers from several hospitals across Metro Manila held a protest dubbed “Kalbaryo ng Manggagawang Pangkalusugan at Mamamayan” in front of the Department of Health (DOH) on Tuesday, March 31, drawing attention to the worsening conditions faced by both medical frontliners and ordinary Filipinos amid a deepening health and economic crisis.

They cited ongoing fuel supply instability as a major factor driving up prices, which in turn has led to a surge in the cost of basic goods and essential services, including medicines, hospitalization, and overall access to healthcare, further compounding the burden on both health workers and the public. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB
